title: Brain activity under anesthesia challenges what we know about consciousness
summary: The unconscious brain appears to be far more capable than scientists once believed. Researchers found that patients under general anesthesia could still process language at a sophisticated level, distinguishing nouns, verbs, and adjectives while listening to stories. The results challenge traditional ideas about consciousness and hint at new possibilities for brain-computer interfaces.

The findings could lead to bio-based treatments that help farmers grow crops on land once considered too salty for agriculture

Drawing on the vastness of the universe and the likely existence of countless alien civilizations, they suggest it would be surprisingly Earth-centric to assume that only Earth-like biology can support conscious experience.

title: Scientists discover ancient brain cells that help block distractions

title: Why South Africa’s leopards shrank to half their normal size

Surprisingly, despite their small population, they have retained much of their genetic diversity.

title: Early humans were bringing fire into caves 1.8 million years ago
